## Core Overview
- Course Code: CSC301 (Design and Analysis of Algorithms)
- Credit Hours: 3(3, 0)
- Pre-Requisite: CSC211-Data Structures
- Primary Purpose: To build core competencies in designing, analyzing, and proving the correctness of efficient algorithms using various paradigms.

## Key Concepts and Formulas
- Asymptotic Notations: Big-O (upper bound), Big-Omega (lower bound), and Big-Theta (tight bound) used for worst, best, and average-case analysis.
- Recurrence Relations: Analyzed using Substitution Method, Recurrence Tree Method, and the Master Method for divide-and-conquer algorithms, such as T(n) = aT(n/2) + f(n).
- Algorithmic Design Paradigms:
  - Brute Force & Decrease-and-Conquer
  - Divide-and-Conquer
  - Transform-and-Conquer
  - Dynamic Programming (e.g., LCS, Knapsack, Edit Distance)
  - Greedy Approach (e.g., Huffman coding/data compression, Coin Change)
- Correctness Proofs: Pre-conditions, post-conditions, loop invariants, and mathematical induction for iterative and recursive algorithms.
- Computability: Complexity classes including P, NP, and an introduction to NP-Complete problems.

## Exam Takeaways
- Complexity Analysis: Master the derivation of time and space complexity using recurrence relation methods (Substitution, Recurrence Tree, Master Theorem).
- Algorithm Design: Be prepared to design and trace algorithms using Dynamic Programming (memoization and tabulation) and Divide-and-Conquer strategies.
- Correctness and Proofs: Memorize loop invariant properties and inductive proof structures for verifying iterative and recursive algorithms.
- Complexity Classes: Understand the formal definitions and distinctions between P, NP, and NP-Complete problem categories.
